name: Yeseul Seo
affiliation: KAIST · Electrical Engineering & Brain and Cognitive Sciences
bio: I'm an undergraduate at KAIST studying Electrical Engineering and Brain and Cognitive Sciences. In Prof. Yang-Kyu Choi's lab, I work on latch-up and hysteresis in SOI transistors using TCAD. Before that, I studied vestibular signal encoding on the DYNAP-SE1 chip at ETH Zürich.
researchStatement: I'm interested in how nonlinear device behavior, particularly latch-up and hysteresis, can be used in neuromorphic circuits. My work has taken me from measuring spike responses on a neuromorphic chip to studying the semiconductor physics behind such systems.
vision: How can we move computation from separate digital blocks into the intrinsic dynamics of devices and circuits?
focus: Single transistor latch in Si device

projects.title: Double-Latch Switching in Divided-Body SOI Transistors
projects.description: I use Silvaco ATLAS to study how two separate latch transitions can arise in a divided-body SOI transistor.
details: Built an SOI structure with two body regions separated by an n+ island and a resistive tap.
Observed latch transitions at 2.254 V and 3.296 V in drift-diffusion simulations.
Tested how doping, island geometry, carrier lifetime, and tap resistance affect the hysteresis.

projects.title: Modeling Human Vestibular Encoding on a Neuromorphic Chip
projects.context: ETH Zürich · Institute of Neuroinformatics · Prof. Giacomo Indiveri / Prof. Elisa Donati
projects.description: At ETH's Institute of Neuroinformatics, I used DYNAP-SE1 to study how vestibular signals are represented by spiking neurons.
details: Applied sinusoidal current directly to the chip instead of using an FPGA-generated input spike train.
Analyzed firing rates, inter-spike intervals, CV, Welch PSD, coherence, and gain.

projects.title: LLM Emotion Control by Vector Steering
projects.context: KAIST · Individual Research · Prof. Sang-Wan Lee
projects.description: I studied whether one language model could influence another model's emotional responses during a multi-turn conversation.
details: Applied hidden-state activation steering to selected transformer layers.
Used emotion classifiers and Bayesian optimization to tune the controller and compare it with prompt-based interventions.

projects.title: Alpha-Synuclein Detection Using Brain Organoids
projects.context: KAIST · Individual Research · Prof. Minee Choi
projects.description: I worked on circular dichroism measurements of α-synuclein in midbrain organoid-conditioned media.
details: Optimized measurements using recombinant α-synuclein controls.
Compared conditions including concentration, dilution, and optical path length.
